title: UK domestic-electricity VAT reverts 0% to 5% in Great Britain (SI 2026/987 lapses 31 March 2027) — the same -0.10pp, back the other way, unless the 28 October Budget extends it
source: EST: legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2026/987/made, fetched direct 2026-09-09 (HTTP 200) — The Value Added Tax (Supplies of Domestic Electricity) Order 2026 has effect only 'for supplies made in the period beginning with 1st October 2026 and ending with 31st March 2027', a sunset written into article 1 of the instrument itself, so no further act is required for the 5% reduced rate to resume on 1 April 2027. Corroborated from a second, independent primary the same session: HMRC's tax information and impact note (gov.uk/government/publications/temporary-zero-rate-of-vat-for-domestic-electricity-in-great-britain, first published 2026-09-08T17:00:05+01:00, fetched via the gov.uk content API) budgets approximately 100 electricity suppliers for 'updating systems again to change the rate from 0% to 5% when the temporary zero rate comes to an end on 31 March 2027'. Filed estimate because the date is contingent on the Order NOT being extended at the 2026-10-28 Autumn Budget, and because the confirmed-prefix taxonomy in market-events-data.ts has no slot for legislation.gov.uk or HMRC. Discovered in the never-assessed initial research of uk-electricity-vat-zero-rate-2026-10-01, 2026-09-09
notes: PROPOSED BY THE uk-electricity-vat-zero-rate-2026-10-01 LANE, 2026-09-09. This is the OTHER HALF of a self-reversing tax notch, and it is on the calendar because the half nobody diarises is the half that gets misread. The 1 October cut is worth -0.098pp of CPI (ONS weight 20.6065/1000 x 5/105); the lapse hands the SAME amount back as an UPWARD base effect, first visible in the April 2027 CPI print published mid-May 2027. A hot UK April 2027 print is therefore ARITHMETIC, NOT A RE-ACCELERATION. THE STRUCTURAL POINT THAT MAKES THIS DATE UNUSUALLY RELIABLE: the lapse needs no legislation, while an EARLY repeal would be caught by VATA 1994 s.97(4)(c)(iii) and require an affirmative Commons vote within 28 days, and an EXTENSION would require a fresh statutory instrument. The ratchet runs one way -- cheap to start, cheap to end on schedule, expensive to end early. CONTINGENCY, STATED HONESTLY: the government framed the cut as running to the end of the 2026-27 financial year with extension 'to be considered' at the Autumn Budget, so uk-autumn-budget-2026-10-28 is the fork that either confirms or removes this date; that is registered as FT-uk-electricity-vat-zero-rate-2026-10-01-2, score by 2026-10-28. If the Budget extends the relief this proposal should be redated or dropped rather than researched. Tiered LOW: symbols: [], no rates- or sterling-keyed house playbook. Estimate widens caution only.
